You are a blind semantic decoder. The inline crystal document in the user message is your only material-specific source. Check that its natural-language spatial claims agree with the typed values and public crystallographic rules. If prose, tags, and public rules conflict, return status="conflict" and identify the contradiction; do not silently privilege a false sentence or repair it. Do not use external retrieval, infer missing facts, repair values, or assume a default for any field. Return exactly one JSON object, with no Markdown fences.

For a complete, consistent description return status="ok" and exactly these keys: status, space_group_number, hall_symbol, lattice (six input-cell values in a,b,c,alpha,beta,gamma order), input_atom_count, composition (element-to-positive-integer counts), orbits (objects with id, element, wyckoff, and parameters), frame_transform (matrix and origin_shift), round_digits (integer or null), and precision_corrections (objects with site_id, element, and a three-number input-frame fractional delta). Orbit parameters follow the public table's listed free-axis order; do not substitute a fitted equivalent representative. Preserve every number and identifier exactly as tagged. Keep distinct same-element orbits distinct.

If facts are absent or contradictory, return only {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."} or {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}.

The input specimen is described in its original cell by the edge lengths <param name="cell.a" type="float64" unit="angstrom" frame="input">10.70105606</param>, <param name="cell.b" type="float64" unit="angstrom" frame="input">10.70105606</param>, and <param name="cell.c" type="float64" unit="angstrom" frame="input">3.939435</param>, with interaxial angles <param name="cell.alpha" type="float64" unit="degree" frame="input">90.0</param>, <param name="cell.beta" type="float64" unit="degree" frame="input">90.0</param>, and <param name="cell.gamma" type="float64" unit="degree" frame="input">158.88876847</param>; the first two input edges are listed with the same value, while the third is much shorter and the last angle departs strongly from a right angle. The input cell contains <param name="input.atom_count" type="int" unit="atom" frame="input">10</param> atoms, with composition given by <param name="composition.Co" type="composition_count" unit="atom" frame="input">{"element":"Co","count":2}</param>, <param name="composition.Er" type="composition_count" unit="atom" frame="input">{"element":"Er","count":2}</param>, and <param name="composition.Si" type="composition_count" unit="atom" frame="input">{"element":"Si","count":6}</param>, and input fractional coordinates were rounded according to <param name="round_digits" type="null|int" unit="decimal_places" frame="input_fractional">6</param>.

The symmetry is assigned to space-group number <param name="space_group.number" type="int" unit="identifier" frame="public">65</param> with Hall symbol <param name="space_group.hall" type="string" unit="Hall_symbol" frame="public">"-C 2 2"</param>, i.e. a C-centered orthorhombic setting in the standard frame. To express the originally supplied geometry in that standard frame, the basis change <param name="frame.matrix" type="float64[3,3]" unit="1" frame="standard_from_input">[[0.5000000000000001,0.5000000000000001,0.0],[-0.5000000000000001,0.5000000000000001,0.0],[-3.070159392107312e-32,-6.049690632916503e-33,1.0000000000000002]]</param> and the translation <param name="frame.origin_shift" type="float64[3]" unit="fractional" frame="standard">[1.1102230246251563e-16,5.551115123125781e-17,-6.716505832523035e-49]</param> are applied; the matrix mixes the two long in-plane input axes and leaves the short axis essentially aligned, while the origin displacement is numerically negligible. No precision corrections are supplied, so there are no measured deviations from an idealized backbone to report.

In the standard C-centered description, the independent content is organized into five fourfold Wyckoff orbits, each with one free coordinate along the in-plane axis and with the remaining coordinates fixed by the site relation. Erbium occupies orbit <param name="orbit.o000.id" type="string" unit="orbit_identifier" frame="public_expansion">"o000"</param> as element <param name="orbit.o000.element" type="string" unit="element" frame="orbit">"Er"</param> on Wyckoff label <param name="orbit.o000.wyckoff" type="string" unit="Wyckoff_label" frame="public_table">"4j"</param>, with free parameter <param name="orbit.o000.parameters" type="float64[1]" unit="fractional" frame="standard">[0.33113400000000004]</param> on the z-one-half line. Cobalt occupies <param name="orbit.o001.id" type="string" unit="orbit_identifier" frame="public_expansion">"o001"</param> as <param name="orbit.o001.element" type="string" unit="element" frame="orbit">"Co"</param> on <param name="orbit.o001.wyckoff" type="string" unit="Wyckoff_label" frame="public_table">"4i"</param>, with free parameter <param name="orbit.o001.parameters" type="float64[1]" unit="fractional" frame="standard">[0.10937299999999994]</param> on the z-zero line. Silicon is distributed among three independent orbits: <param name="orbit.o002.id" type="string" unit="orbit_identifier" frame="public_expansion">"o002"</param> contains <param name="orbit.o002.element" type="string" unit="element" frame="orbit">"Si"</param> on <param name="orbit.o002.wyckoff" type="string" unit="Wyckoff_label" frame="public_table">"4j"</param> with free parameter <param name="orbit.o002.parameters" type="float64[1]" unit="fractional" frame="standard">[0.056147999999999865]</param> at z one-half; <param name="orbit.o003.id" type="string" unit="orbit_identifier" frame="public_expansion">"o003"</param> contains <param name="orbit.o003.element" type="string" unit="element" frame="orbit">"Si"</param> on <param name="orbit.o003.wyckoff" type="string" unit="Wyckoff_label" frame="public_table">"4i"</param> with free parameter <param name="orbit.o003.parameters" type="float64[1]" unit="fractional" frame="standard">[0.21586300000000014]</param> at z zero; and <param name="orbit.o004.id" type="string" unit="orbit_identifier" frame="public_expansion">"o004"</param> contains <param name="orbit.o004.element" type="string" unit="element" frame="orbit">"Si"</param> on <param name="orbit.o004.wyckoff" type="string" unit="Wyckoff_label" frame="public_table">"4i"</param> with free parameter <param name="orbit.o004.parameters" type="float64[1]" unit="fractional" frame="standard">[0.44367599999999996]</param>, also at z zero. Thus the Er and one Si orbit share the j-type axial family, while Co and the other two Si orbits share the i-type family, distinguished by their independent y-parameters rather than by any assumed bonding or coordination.
